concept: Bucket-level predicate rewriting for measurement operators
summary: Source-anchored research for Bucket-level predicate rewriting for measurement operators. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: MongoDB's 2026 SERVER-126494 report reproduces an incorrect result when a measurement field contains NaN and an aggregation applies $match {v: {$lt: 50}} followed by an inclusion $project: the regular collection returns {v: 1}, but the time-series collection returns no row. Jira lists 9.1.0-rc0 as the fix version. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-29)

MongoDB Jira recorded historical false negatives when buckets mixed array and scalar values or mixed objects and non-objects on measurement paths; SERVER-59505 is marked fixed in 5.0.4, 5.1.0-rc3, and 5.2.0. SERVER-60565 describes splitting buckets when an incoming measurement has an incompatible schema. (high confidence) Sources: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-59505 ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-60565

The generator declines object, array, and null operands; non-default-collation string comparisons; computed or removed fields; and non-time internal LT/LTE comparisons without type bracketing. When mixed schema cannot be ruled out, it adds a type-equality fallback across control.min/control.max path prefixes. SERVER-59505 records earlier false negatives when array/scalar or object/scalar values shared a bucket. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-22) Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/query/timeseries/bucket_level_comparison_predicate_generator.cpp ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-59505

For non-time measurement fields, MongoDB treats the min/max predicate as a candidate filter rather than proof that every measurement matches. The generator disables a tight predicate because missing measurement values are omitted from control summaries and array-valued controls can change comparison semantics; MongoDB's query notes say individual measurements are still filtered after bucket selection. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-22) Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/query/timeseries/bucket_level_comparison_predicate_generator.cpp ; https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/query/timeseries/README.md

Starting in MongoDB 6.0, a $match on a non-time measurement field can add a bucket filter to the COLLSCAN or FETCH: equality uses control.min <= value and control.max >= value; $gt/$gte compare against control.max; and $lt/$lte compare against control.min. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-22) Sources: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/query/timeseries/README.md ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/query/timeseries/bucket_level_comparison_predicate_generator.cpp

For the special timeField path, the generator only uses the bucket comparison rewrite for BSON Date operands; comparing the time field to a non-Date type is declined, because users cannot insert non-Date values into the time field so such a query would not match anything. Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/query/timeseries/bucket_level_comparison_predicate_generator.cpp

Percona's MongoDB 5.0 time series example shows summary-field filters (control.max.timestamp and control.min.timestamp) generated for a timestamp comparison only; it is context for bucket pruning, not a test of measurement-field predicates. Sources: https://www.percona.com/blog/mongodb-5-0-time-series-collections/

MongoDB's manual says that grouping documents by matching metaField values and close timeField values narrows the scope of a query to a range of buckets. Separately, MongoDB Jira (SERVER-59505) shows that predicates on measurement fields are pushed down to the bucket collection as comparisons on the bucket's control.min/control.max summary fields. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-querying/ ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-59505
